torchcompile is faster based on my benchmark script

w/ torch.compile
```
{
```

without torch.compile
```
{
    "model": "tiny_vit_21m_224",
    "infer_samples_per_sec": 5223.06,
    "infer_step_time": 49.0,
    "infer_batch_size": 256,
    "infer_img_size": 224,
    "train_samples_per_sec": 1554.02,
    "train_step_time": 164.429,
    "train_batch_size": 256,
    "train_img_size": 224,
    "param_count": 33.22
}
```

And simple fine-tune on resisc45 yielded same results w/ and w/o torch.compile... I don't use fullgraph=True though by default, but if there's a difference there it's not a timm issue, it's a torch issue. I used PyTorch 2.9.1. I had numerous issues w/ torch.compile + AMP (though usually also with DDP) on PyTorch 2.8 and 2.7 that don't exist in 2.5 and 2.9.x.

resisc 45 fine-tune w/ same pretrained model:

comments.body:
One additional thing I just tested as well was compiling the full train step:
```python
def train_step(inputs, labels):
    optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
    with torch.amp.autocast(device_type="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
        pred = model(inputs)
        loss = criterion(pred, labels)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    return loss

train_step = torch.compile(train_step)
```
But that did not lead to any meaningful speed improvements
